steps.say: The practice house! Helping at home is a superpower. Today, with Gus: the washing, the bedroom, a plant, Biscuit the dog, the recycling and the smoke alarm.

lines.w_shirt: A white T-shirt: into the whites basket.

steps.say: Sort the washing: white things go in one basket, colours in the other. Touch each white thing.
steps.done: Whites with whites, colours with colours, so no colour runs onto the whites.

steps.say: Sort the washing: touch all four white things.
steps.done: All four whites, by yourself.

not.sock_spot_a: That one has spots: look for red stripes.
not.sock_spot_b: That one has spots: look for red stripes.

steps.say: Bobo's red striped sock needs its partner. Touch the other red striped sock.
steps.done: A pair! Pairs of socks go in the drawer together.

steps.say: Fold the T-shirt: one sleeve in, the other sleeve in, then fold it in half.
steps.done: Neatly folded, ready for the drawer.

lines.toy_car: The car goes home: the toy box.
lines.book: The book goes home: the shelf.

steps.say: Tidy up: everything has a home. Touch each thing on the floor to put it back in its home.
steps.done: Everything in its home, so it's easy to find next time.

lines.shoes: Shoes go home: the shoe rack.

steps.say: Tidy up: put all four things back in their homes.
steps.done: All tidy, by yourself.

steps.say: Water the plant: hold the watering can over it until the soil is damp, not soaking.
steps.done: Just right: damp soil, happy roots.

steps.say: When does a plant need water?

choices.why: Too much water hurts a plant too. Feel the soil first: dry means water.

steps.done: Feel the soil: dry means water.

steps.say: Biscuit is hungry. Pour his food into his bowl: touch the bowl.
steps.done: Crunch, crunch! Dogs eat at the same times each day.

steps.say: And fresh water, every day: pour it into his water bowl.
steps.done: Fresh, clean water: Biscuit always needs it.

steps.say: What else does Biscuit need?

choices.text: A walk and a clean bed

choices.why: Dogs need the right food, fresh water, walks and a clean bed. Sweets can make them poorly.

steps.done: Walks and a cosy, clean bed. And a vet when he's poorly.

not.bin_glass: That's for glass jars and bottles. Look for the paper picture.
not.bin_food: That's for food scraps. Look for the paper picture.

steps.say: Recycling: things go in their own bins, so they can be made into new things. An old newspaper: touch the PAPER bin.
steps.done: Paper in the paper bin. It can become new paper!

not.bin_paper: Paper only in that one. Look for the bottle picture.
not.bin_glass: That's for glass. Look for the bottle picture.
not.bin_food: That's for food scraps. Look for the bottle picture.

steps.say: An empty plastic bottle: which bin? Look for the bottle picture.
steps.done: In the PLASTIC AND CANS bin.

steps.say: With Gus: press and hold the smoke alarm's test button until it beeps.
steps.done: BEEP! It works. Gus tests it with you once a month.

steps.say: What a helper! Whites and colours, socks in pairs, folding, everything in its home, a watered plant, a happy Biscuit, the recycling and the smoke alarm.

lines: Whites with whites, colours with colours; socks in pairs; fold sleeves in, then in half.
Everything has a home: put things back.
Water a plant when its soil feels dry. A pet needs food, fresh water, walks, a clean bed, and a vet when poorly.

little.try_real: Choose one job at home to do every week, like pairing the socks or feeding a pet with your grown-up. And find your smoke alarm together: watch your grown-up press its test button.

sources.fact: Pets have five welfare needs: a suitable place to live, the right food and fresh water, to behave normally (walks and play for a dog), company, and protection from pain and illness (a vet when they're poorly).

sources.fact: Test your smoke alarm by pressing its test button once a month.

lines: Sort the washing (no red sock in the whites) and fold it flat.

steps.say: For older helpers: washing labels, the washing machine, folding and putting away, the dishwasher, batteries, plants on holiday and the smoke alarm.
Clothes have a care label of symbols: a tub is washing, a triangle bleach, a square drying, an iron ironing, a circle dry cleaning. A cross over one means no.
This T-shirt's label shows a tub with 30 in it. You wash it at...

choices.text: As hot as the machine goes
choices.why: The number is the hottest wash it can take, in degrees: hotter can shrink it or fade it.

steps.done: 30 degrees at most.

steps.say: This towel's label shows a tub with 40 in it. You wash it at...

choices.why: The number is the hottest wash it can take, in degrees.

steps.done: 40 degrees at most, by yourself.

steps.say: The woolly jumper's label shows a hand in the tub: hand wash only. You...

choices.text: Wash it gently by hand, in cool water

choices.why: A hand in the tub means hand wash: a hot machine wash can shrink wool.

steps.done: Gently by hand.

steps.say: A square with a circle inside, crossed out, means...

choices.text: Don't tumble dry it: dry it flat or on a line

choices.why: The square with a circle is the tumble dryer; the cross means no.

steps.done: No tumble dryer for that one.

steps.say: Load the drum and close the door; with Gus watching, turn the dial to the 30 programme; then press START.
steps.done: Washing at 30. Gus put the powder in the drawer.

steps.done: Folded and put away.

steps.say: The dishwasher: scraped plates in the bottom rack, then a cup upside down on the top rack.
steps.done: Plates down below, cups on top.

not.slot_up: Sharp points up could hurt a hand reaching in: sharp knives go point down.

steps.done: Point down: nobody's hand meets a sharp point.

not.slot_up: Sharp points up could hurt a hand reaching in: sharp knives go point down.

steps.say: The sharp knife: which way into the basket?
steps.done: Point down, by yourself.

steps.say: How often do you test a smoke alarm?

choices.why: Once a month, so you know it will warn you.

steps.done: Once a month.

name_it.title: Labels, knives, batteries, alarms
lines: The care label: a tub with a number is the hottest wash; a hand is hand wash; a crossed-out square with a circle is no tumble dryer.
The dishwasher: plates below, cups on top, sharp knives point down.
Batteries never go in the bins: a battery box at a shop.
Test the smoke alarm once a month; never take its battery out.
name_it.source: GINETEX's care symbols (ISO 3758), the fire and rescue services, the appliance makers' safety advice and Recycle Now

big.try_real: With a grown-up, read the care labels of three of your clothes, then load the dishwasher or the washing machine together. Ask them to show you where your home's battery box or battery recycling is.

sources.fact: Care labels: the number in the washing tub is the highest temperature in degrees; a bar under it means a gentler wash; a hand means hand wash; a square with a circle is tumble drying (crossed out: don't); the iron's dots show its heat.
Load knives and other sharp utensils in the cutlery basket with their points down (or flat, where the maker allows) to prevent injury; keep children from handling them.
Never put batteries in the household bins: they can cause fires in bin lorries and recycling centres; take them to a battery collection point (many shops have one).
sources.source: Recycle Your Electricals (Material Focus) and Recycle Now

sources.fact: Test smoke alarms monthly; a regular chirp usually means the battery is low: replace it, never remove it.
sources.source: NFPA, smoke alarms; the London Fire Brigade

sources.fact: Before going away, ask a neighbour to water plants, or stand them in trays of water; group them out of direct sun.
sources.source: the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), holiday watering
